title: KV sticky failover and SLO degradation inspector hotpatch
author: Arjun Menon
release_notes: Hotfix: improve cross-zone failover to preserve per-request KV cache when routing falls back; add SLO Degradation Inspector to prevent premature circuit reopen and surface tenant-level SLO drift by route.
description:
Context and motivation: A recent incident (SUP-817) showed repeated cross-zone failovers causing mass KV cache invalidation, which amplified token latency and triggered SLO regressions for a small set of high-throughput tenants. The root cause was an aggressive circuit reopen path combined with global KV flush semantics during transparent fallback. This patch provides a fast hotfix with three coordinated pieces: 1) a 'KV sticky fallback' mode that preserves per-request KV/ prefix caches for short windowed failovers (configurable TTL), 2) a SLO Degradation Inspector service that computes lightweight per-tenant SLO drift and gates circuit state transitions, and 3) a conservative reopen backoff tweak for the regional circuit breaker to avoid oscillation.

Change summary (single-string):
- Introduced kv/sticky_fallback.go: implements a short-lived sticky reservation of KV prefixes when a request is redirected to a fallback model variant or region; ensures most recent KV entries are shadow-copied to the fallback path for the rescue window. Config options: sticky_window_ms, max_shadow_bytes_per_tenant.
- Added inspector/slo_degradation_inspector.go: background probe that samples per-route latency and error percentiles (p50/p95/err-rate) and exposes a DegradationScore used by the circuit manager to delay reopen when score > threshold.
- Modified circuit/region_breaker.go: integrate DegradationScore check into reopen path and apply exponential reopen backoff with jitter.
- Telemetry: added metrics slo_degradation.score, kv_sticky.shadow_hits, kv_sticky.shadow_misses, kv_sticky.shadow_bytes; added events for "sticky_assigned" and "sticky_released".
- Tests: unit + integration harness updates for sticky fallback scenarios and inspector thresholds; added a load test script used in the incident runbook.

Design notes and constraints: sticky_fallback is intentionally conservative: shadow copies are bounded per-tenant, stored in memory on the node handling the fallback, and expire after sticky_window_ms. The design avoids persistent cross-node replication to prevent cascading capacity pressure. The Degradation Inspector samples lightweight histograms (not full traces) to keep CPU cost low and only affects circuit reopen decisions (it is read-only; failures default to permissive behavior after a safe timeout).

Review conversation (selected threads, single-string):
- Maya Patel (reviewer): "Nice focused hotfix. Two asks: (1) please add a circuit manager metric for how often the DegradationInspector blocks reopen so we can confirm effectiveness; (2) ensure shadow copy size is configurable per-tenant (some tenants have large KV footprints)."
- Arjun (author): "Added metric slo_degradation.block_count and tenant-scoped max_shadow_bytes with default 4MB. Updated tests to validate tenant override."
- Elena Ruiz (reviewer): "Can we add a safety-to-fallback mode: if inspector service becomes unavailable, we should default to a short safe delay rather than immediate reopen. Otherwise risk noisy reopen when inspector is down."
- Arjun (author): "Implemented inspector health-check and default-delay of 2000ms when inspector is unavailable. Documented in runbook."
- Tom Becker (reviewer): "LGTM after nits. Would like an independent canary rollout to 10% of traffic in staging before prod." 
- Arjun (author): "Canary rollout planned; added rollout config and a staging canary job in CI."

CI summary: initial pipeline (unit + linters) passed; integration step failed on first run due to test harness timing (flaky loadtest). Fixed test timing and re-ran; full pipeline passed. e2e-staging run completed with canary routing to 10% for 2 hours and showed 61% reduction in failover-induced p95 delta for the affected tenant in staging.

Observability and post-merge runbook: docs/operational/kv-sticky-fallback.md includes commands to inspect sticky assignments, release them, and force a graceful release for a tenant. Dashboard names: "SLO Inspector - Degradation Score", "KV Sticky - Shadow Hit Rate". Suggested post-merge monitoring window: 48 hours with alerting on slo_degradation.score > 50 or kv_sticky.shadow_bytes > 80% configured budget.

Rollout and rollback plan: squash-merged to main and cherry-picked into release/2026-02 with a small canary (10%) for 2 hours then gradual ramp. Rollback is a single revert of the squash commit (documented) or temporary setting sticky_window_ms=0 to disable sticky mode quickly.

Merge outcome: merged into main via squash on 2026-02-17 after approvals from all reviewers.
notes: This PR is targeted at runtime reliability; considered low-risk but urgent. The change is intentionally narrow and guarded by inspector metrics and a small default sticky window.
